snapshot: Outside WHO since 22 January 2026. Global health now runs through the State Department's America First strategy: 36 bilateral agreements, with US$15.9 billion from the US and US$10.3 billion in partner co-investment (KFF, October 2026). At home, the Health Department under Robert F. Kennedy Jr. rewrote vaccine policy, largely stayed in court, and the US lost its measles elimination status in November 2026.

agenda.title: America First bilateral health agreements
agenda.text: 36 agreements signed by October 2026, mostly in Africa but also in Latin America and Asia, for 2026 to 2030: US$15.9 billion from the US and US$10.3 billion in co-investment, while five-year funding for these countries falls by about a third. Most texts are unpublished; several oblige partners to share outbreak specimens and data with the US. Some, such as Nigeria and Uganda, prioritise faith-based providers. South Africa has none and PEPFAR there is being closed out; Ghana and Zimbabwe turned the terms down.

agenda.title: Outside WHO, with its own health security tools
agenda.text: The US left WHO and rejected the revised International Health Regulations. For Ebola it relies on entry restrictions: since May it bars non-citizens, including green-card holders, who were recently in affected countries, and from 3 November every US-bound air passenger must declare no stay in the DR Congo in the previous 21 days (order runs to 18 December).

agenda.title: Vaccine policy in court
agenda.text: In January 2026 the CDC, without its advisory committee, cut the diseases covered by universal childhood vaccination recommendations from 17 to 11. On 16 March a federal judge stayed those changes and the reconstituted advisory committee (ACIP); the government appealed to the First Circuit. ACIP had not met since December 2025 as of mid-2026, and several states follow medical societies' own schedules.

agenda.title: Measles: elimination status lost
agenda.text: A PAHO commission found that measles has circulated for more than 12 months, ending the elimination status the US held since 2000; Mexico and Bolivia lost theirs too, after Canada last year. CDC counted 5,412 cases in 2026 by 12 November. CDC and partners announced a plan to regain elimination with US$100 million for health departments.

agenda.title: Budget for global health in 2027
agenda.text: The President asked US$5.1 billion for the main global health account for fiscal 2027, US$4.3 billion below 2026. The House committee bill has US$8.9 billion; the Senate committee released its bills on 16 November. Congress keeps PEPFAR and the Global Fund funded, and the new Congress elected on 3 November takes office in January.
